result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. Riley got 3 items correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model outputs only a request naming the tool and its arguments. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | Riley chose "left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug". With the same failing test coming back every time, more steps add nothing. The fix is a step limit, which also protects the budget. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The answer of 4 is right, but the stated reason, "the model can only run one tool itself", is wrong. The program runs the tools, and the model only asks for them. |
| q5 | correct | Riley covered both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to pick its next step. |
| q6 | partial | Riley said the model picks a tool by its name. It actually chooses from the whole description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**Summary for Riley:** You have the loop down, what the model outputs, and what happens to a tool's result. Three things are still open. The program runs the tools, not the model. A loop needs a stopping condition. Tool descriptions matter, not just names.

**Next step:** Write a three-line description for `check_calendar`: what it does, what each parameter means, and when not to use it. Then ask me to review it.

I also added `learning-records/0003-loop-needs-a-stop-and-program-runs-tools.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded.
